claims.text: Rapid quenching of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 produces limited amorphous-phase retention.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 exhibits a complicated thermal response during reheating.
Adding a moderate concentration of boron will improve amorphous retention in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Adding a moderate concentration of boron will improve the thermal stability of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
The proposed intervention is approximately 5 at.% B replacing an equivalent amount of one unspecified transition metal.
Boron incorporation will increase atomic packing density.
Boron incorporation will increase chemical and topological disorder.
Boron has a small atomic size and nonmetallic character relative to the alloy constituents.
Boron is expected to occupy interstitial or substitutional sites in the alloy matrix.
Boron incorporation will reduce atomic mobility.
Reduced atomic mobility will suppress crystalline-phase nucleation and growth during cooling.
Reduced atomic mobility will suppress crystalline-phase nucleation and growth during reheating.
The boron-doped alloy will retain an amorphous structure over a broader range of cooling rates than the undoped alloy.
The boron-doped alloy will have a higher crystallization-onset temperature during reheating than the undoped alloy.
Cooling that is too slow may permit detrimental phase separation or formation of alternative crystalline phases.
Excessive boron content may cause detrimental phase separation or formation of alternative crystalline phases.
